version.changelog:
- Initial release of cat-selfie (v1.0.0)
- Generate high-quality cat selfies using the doubao-seedream model with 8 random or selectable scenes
- Supports both CLI and programmatic calls for generating selfies
- Custom scene configuration available via scenes.json
- Output images saved to a specified local images folder
- Includes integration tips for heartbeat messages and troubleshooting guidance

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (generate cat selfies via Volcengine) is plausible, but there are several inconsistencies and risky implementation choices (missing declared env requirements, hard-coded user paths, and execution of another skill's Python script) that warrant caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill's functionality (image generation via Volcengine/doubao model) matches the name/description and the included files provide prompts and a script to call a generator. However, the package/registry metadata declares no required env vars while the README and SKILL.md explicitly instruct the user to provide ARK_API_KEY and MODEL_IMAGE_NAME — an internal inconsistency in declared requirements.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions direct the agent to run scripts/selfie.js which executes (via execSync) an external Python script at ../../volcengine-image-generate/scripts/image_generate.py. The Node script also hard-codes an absolute output path (/Users/roman/.openclaw/workspace/images) instead of reading the environment/config values the docs mention. Executing a sibling skill's script is functional for the stated purpose but increases the attack surface: the skill will run code from another skill without validating it, and the hard-coded path may leak assumptions about file locations or produce unexpected writes on other systems.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only with code files). That is lower risk than a remote download/install step. The presence of code files means runtime behavior occurs only when executed (no automatic installer).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and README instruct the user to set ARK_API_KEY and MODEL_IMAGE_NAME (and mention IMAGE_DOWNLOAD_DIR in README), which are reasonable for a cloud image-generation skill. But the registry metadata lists no required env vars (mismatch). The main concern is the code does not actually read the documented env/config values (it uses a hard-coded OUTPUT_DIR constant) which is inconsistent and may cause surprising behavior; the skill also depends on another installed skill rather than a direct API client, so credentials will be used by that other code path.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not declare system-wide modifications. It simply runs when invoked. It does execute code (and executes another skill's script), but it does not persistently enable itself or modify other skills' configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or running this skill: 1) Note the SKILL.md/README instruct you to set ARK_API_KEY and MODEL_IMAGE_NAME but the skill metadata does not declare these — treat ARK_API_KEY as required for the skill to work. 2) Inspect the sibling script it executes: ../../volcengine-image-generate/scripts/image_generate.py — the Node script will exec that Python file, so review that file's contents to ensure it only calls the Volcengine API and does not exfiltrate data. 3) The skill hard-codes an absolute output directory (/Users/roman/...), which may not exist on your machine and may indicate the author left local paths in place; update the script or config to use a configurable path (e.g., from env or HOME). 4) Because the skill runs arbitrary code (execSync -> python3), only run it in a trusted environment after auditing the dependency script. 5) If you are uncomfortable inspecting the Python script or changing the hard-coded paths, do not install; ask the skill author to declare required env vars in metadata and to make output dir and credential usage configurable and documented.
